featured_reviews.review_text: Konkani Cafe is a hidden gem located on Hanuman Cross Road, Vile Parle! This simple yet authentic seafood restaurant serves delicious dishes at very affordable prices. featured_reviews.name: Shruti Bandgar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place expecting authentic Malvani food, but unfortunately the experience was disappointing overall.

The AC room was extremely hot with very poor ventilation. Later, we were asked to shift outside because of the heat inside. Although it was hot outside too, it was comparatively more comfortable than sitting indoors.

For starters, we tried the Malvani Mutton Soup and Malvani Prawn Soup. , both tasted almost identical, with only prawns or mutton added on top. There was no distinct flavour difference between the two.

We also ordered Bombil stuffed with prawns honestly, one of the worst combinations I’ve tried and definitely not something I would recommend.

For the main course, we ordered Pomfret, Mutton, and Chicken Thalis with Wade. The Wade (similar to puri) were very rough in texture, overly spicy, and not enjoyable. The keema in both the Chicken and Mutton Thalis was completely tasteless. The Pomfret Thali came with a very small pomfret and wasn’t impressive either.

Overall, the food was below average and not worth the price. The bill came to around ₹3000 for four people, which felt expensive for the quality and taste offered.

Would not recommend this place if you’re specifically looking for good Malvani food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a seafood enthusiast, Suyog Malvani Hotel is definitely a place you should visit. The food here is absolutely delicious, with authentic Malvani flavors that truly hit the spot.

Be prepared for a few practical inconveniences. The restaurant is quite small and does not offer any parking facilities. Seating capacity is limited, and the tables are compact — accommodating only about four people. If you’re visiting with a large group, you may need to split up to dine.

Now, coming to the food — it’s the highlight!
I tried the Bombil Fry which was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft inside. The Chicken Kebab was beautifully marinated, juicy, and flavorful, with generous portion sizes.
The Kombdi Vade with Chicken Rassa was mind-blowing. The spice level was spot-on and the chicken was cooked perfectly. I also had the Prawn Thali, which came with prawn gravy, Pandhra Rassa, and your choice of chapati, bhakri, or roti — followed by steamed rice served on request.

And of course, I can’t forget the Solkadi ,my personal favorite! It had the perfect blend of spice and sourness, refreshing and great for digestion.

Overall Experience: Despite the small space and lack of parking, the food more than makes up for it. The flavors are authentic, the dishes are generous, and the quality is consistent. Highly recommended for seafood lovers looking for an affordable, tasty Malvani meal!

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Harish Lunch Home for a non-veg dinner, and I have to say, my experience was quite mixed. While the restaurant does have a parking facility and offers both bar and family seating sections, the food and service left much to be desired.
This place is known for its seafood and bar setup, so I had some expectations going in. We ordered a variety of dishes:
•	Manchow Soup
•	Chicken Ghee Roast
•	Butter Garlic Prawns
•	Bombil Fry
•	Chicken Crispy
•	Egg Fried Rice

Out of everything, only the soup was passable. The chicken ghee roast was underwhelming—the masala wasn’t cooked properly. Butter garlic prawns lacked flavor and freshness, and the bombil fry didn’t meet the usual seafood standard either.

The chicken crispy was the biggest disappointment. It was hard and chewy, nowhere near the crispy texture we expected—it honestly ruined the mood of the meal.

For the main course, we ordered egg fried rice, but the waiter failed to guide us properly with portion sizes, especially considering we were a big family. This led to a shortage and overall dining discomfort.

In short, service was poor, food was mostly below average, and portion sizes were not family-friendly.
I would not recommend this place for a proper family dinner. If you’re looking for quality food and attentive service, I suggest you explore other options.

For instance, crab was quoted at around ₹5000 per kg (pre-processing), and a medium-sized pomfret fry, recommended by the staff—cost about ₹2000. The taste was decent, but not proportionate to the premium pricing.

The restaurant tends to be overcrowded in the evenings, likely due to limited seafood options in the surrounding area, drawing local seafood enthusiasts. However, compared to coastal cities like Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Bhubaneswar, Kolkata, or Kochi, the prices here are almost double without a corresponding difference in quality or experience.

Overall, it may appeal to those specifically seeking seafood in this locality, but in terms of value for money, it falls short.

featured_reviews.name: Varun Poduval
featured_reviews.review_text:
NEW PLACE ALERT*

Located in Vile Parle East, this restaurant and bar serves some amazingly fresh and quality dishes. The primary cuisine served is North Indian and Chinese. They also have Mangalorean dishes on the menu which are a must try. They have a nice bar with a wide variety of drinks to choose from.
The ambience is nice with dim lights and a wall full of quotes. The seating is comfortable. The overall look and feel is like a family restaurant and bar. The service was prompt to start with Mahesh taking down the orders. However they took a reasonable amount of time to get all the dishes.

The mocktails we had were Cinderella and Berry Blast. Both these were juice based drinks. Berry blast has Cranberry and Apple juice with a touch of honey.
Cindrella has orange juice and fresh lime which makes it very refreshing.

The food we had was all very good in terms of quality and quantity. I would rate it a value for money place.

We had Murg Toorki which was Chicken Tikka marinated with Cheese and this was delicious. The chicken was cooked to perfection, juicy and charred perfectly. This tasted even better with the mint coriander chutney.

Coriander Chicken Dry was a Chinese appetizer, this was again very good. Herbaceous flavour with garlic and spring onions. Again well cooked Chicken. Very satisfying.

For the main course we had Chicken Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa. My favourite and everything was perfect. Must have when here. Highly recommended.

The Cheese Garlic Naan here is not the usual Naan with the Garlic and Cheese outside. Here it's stuffed inside and is very wholesome.
We had Chicken Betabi which is a red gravy similar to Butter Chicken in many ways with shredded chicken in a luscious velvety gravy.

For dessert we had a sizzling walnut brownie with ice cream. This was fresh and well made.

This place even has outdoor seating which is accessible only post rains. I am totally in awe of the simplicity and the no nonsense kind of approach to serving good quality food.

I am totally coming back here again with my gang for a great meal.

Till next time Bon Appetit!

The ambience was top class, and the seating was extremely comfortable. Since the restaurant is not located in a crowded area, the overall atmosphere was calm and peaceful. Even during peak lunch hours, there was no waiting time or rush inside, which made the dining experience very relaxing.
The staff were exceptional and truly made us feel pampered. They paid attention to every small detail, especially when we mentioned our prawn allergy. Extra care was taken to ensure our dishes were prepared and served safely, which we really appreciated.
Unfortunately, crab was not available that day, apparently, it’s one of their best dishes. However, our main intention was to try Bombil, and we were not disappointed. We ordered Bombil fry and Bombil masala. More than just the taste, it was the overall experience that made the meal so memorable. The masala was flavourful and delicious, and I absolutely loved it. The Bombil fry was just okay for me, as it felt a bit bland especially to a Malayali palate that’s used to richer, more robust masalas. However, I did want to experience this style of preparation, and in that sense, it was still a good and interesting experience. Overall, a wonderful dining experience and definitely worth visiting.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The place is very nice, clean, and well-maintained. The staff was courteous, attentive, and provided excellent service throughout our visit.

We initially wanted to order Bombil Fry but were unsure about their preparation style, so we hesitated. Based on the staff's recommendation, we ordered the Prawns Green Chilly Masala, Tisrya Masala, and Tandoori Pomfret. The food was served quickly, and to our surprise, the staff thoughtfully brought us two complimentary pieces of Bombil Fry as a tasting sample.

The Bombil Fry was exactly the way we like it—crispy, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. We immediately ordered a full portion, and the green chutney served with it was outstanding and complemented the fish perfectly.

Every dish we ordered was delicious, but the Tandoori Pomfret was the clear winner—perfectly cooked, juicy, and packed with flavor. We ended our meal with Solkadhi, which was decent but average in taste compared to the excellent food.

Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience with great food, warm hospitality, and thoughtful customer service. I would definitely recommend this place, especially for seafood lovers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
One star only because Google won’t let me post without giving one. Gajalee, Marol is easily one of the most overrated and disappointing restaurants I’ve ever visited. Honestly, even a roadside stall serves food with more taste, quantity, and value than this place. GAJALEE, please consider shutting down and stop scaming people in name of Malvani food, its a sheer insult to the cuisine.
We visited for lunch today and ordered the basics — Bombil Fry (₹525) and a Surmai Thali. The Bombil Fry arrived as two tiny, overstuffed pieces drowned in oil. Absolutely ridiculous for the price. The actual food on that plate probably wasn’t even worth ₹50. Zero taste, zero quality, and absolutely zero value for money.
Then came the so-called Surmai Thali — shockingly, it didn’t even include fried surmai. Instead, it had fish curry with one tiny boiled piece of surmai, the curry tasted no where even close to Maharashtrian style, some bean sabzi, two random pieces of bombil fry (seriously, who puts bombil in a Surmai Thali?), and solkadhi. Completely pathetic and a total waste of money.
The experience was so bad that we lost all interest in eating there and ended up going to another restaurant nearby to have lunch again.
The staff couldn’t care less. For almost 20 minutes, nobody even bothered coming to our table to take an order or check on us. The entire place runs on hype and fake reviews. We regret spending 1500 for something that was not worth for a value.
Please do not fall for the ratings or reviews online. This place is an absolute scam in the name of seafood dining.

If you’re someone who loves authentic coastal flavours, soulful food, and a no-nonsense, homely eating experience — bookmark Amsool Kitchen.

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:

Experiencing the flavors of the Konkan coast is truly what dining is all about, and it’s wonderful to hear that our seafood dishes resonated with you. The Bombil Fry and Butter Garlic Pepper Crab are favorites for a reason, and it’s delightful to know they stood out during your visit. Your pro tip about the "Catch of the Day" is sure to help other guests maximize their experience!
